How does this page rank Higgsfield alternatives?

This page ranks sites like Higgsfield by the dollars-per-second rows in our catalog, then compares the same model side by side so a cheap row for a different model is not treated as a like-for-like saving. A credit-plan figure assumes you use the credits you pay for; unused credits make the real cost higher. An API figure is billed per second of output, at the resolution and audio the vendor published. Higgsfield is an affiliate; those links never change this price order. Related: cheapest Wan 3.0 · best AI video generator by value.

Which option is best for each use?

Best-for lines are given only where a catalog row or a vendor page supports them. Higgsfield Ultra (annual) is best for the lowest catalog rate we track on Wan 3.0, Wan 3.0 Prime, Kling 3.0, and Hailuo 2.3, if you use every paid credit. It is not for Veo 3.1 Lite, where Krea is cheaper, or for Seedance 2.5 on a Higgsfield plan, because that plan rate is not in the catalog. Krea Basic (yearly) is best for Veo 3.1 Lite cost in the catalog. Replicate is best for Seedance 2.5 at 480p with no video input among the rows we can compare. No line is given for OpenArt cost per second, because credits per clip were not published on the public pricing page we read.

  • Higgsfield Ultra (annual). Best for: the lowest catalog rate we track on Wan 3.0, Wan 3.0 Prime, Kling 3.0, and Hailuo 2.3, if you use every paid credit. Not for: Veo 3.1 Lite, where Krea is cheaper; Seedance 2.5 on a plan rate we can show; or pay-as-you-go without a monthly plan. Higgsfield’s pricing page. Related: Higgsfield pricing.
  • Krea Basic (yearly). Best for: Veo 3.1 Lite cost in the catalog. Not for: Wan 3.0, where Higgsfield is cheaper. Krea’s pricing page.
  • Replicate. Best for: Seedance 2.5 at 480p with no video input, among the rows we can compare. Not for: Wan 3.0, where Higgsfield’s plan rate is lower.

No line given for OpenArt cost per second, or for a Higgsfield plan rate on Seedance 2.5, Gemini Omni Flash, or Runway Gen-4, because those per-second figures are not in the catalog or were not published on the pages we could verify.

What free Higgsfield alternatives are there?

Higgsfield lists a Free plan with 0 monthly credits and limited access to selected models; how many complimentary generations it actually allows, and which models are in that set, is unknown. Official pages that do publish a countable free text-to-video allowance are covered in our free-tier guides: Google Flow (50 credits a day) and Krea Free (100 compute units a day, no card). Kling lists a $0 Basic plan but does not publish credits per clip. OpenArt’s public pricing page, read today, did not publish a free-plan credit allotment, so that figure is unknown. See free AI video generators: what you get and free text to video AI.

How does Higgsfield compare with OpenArt on price?

OpenArt’s public pricing page, read today, lists four individual plans per seat: Starter $14 a month for 4,000 credits, Plus $34 for 12,000, Pro $56 for 24,000, and Wonder $240 for 106,000. The same page’s structured data lists annual billed rates of $13, $27, $44, and $175 a month. The visible cards also show a first-year annual promotional price ($11, $24, $36, and $144 a month). OpenArt says promotional discounts apply only to the first billing period and that the plan then renews at the then-current list price. Credits per clip for Wan, Kling, Veo, or Hailuo are not on that public page, so an OpenArt dollars-per-second figure is unknown and is not shown. Starter has no commercial-use right in the structured data; Plus and higher do. Higgsfield’s catalog Starter is $19 a month for 270 credits, checked Nov 17, 2026 PT. OpenArt’s pricing page, read Nov 17, 2026, 4:50–4:53 PM America/Caracas (12:50–12:53 PM PT).

What is confirmed, and what is not?

Confirmed today from the catalog (last full check 2026-11-17): the platform and same-model rows in the tables, including Higgsfield Ultra (annual) plan math at $50/month for 3,000 credits. Confirmed today on OpenArt’s pricing page: the monthly and annual list prices, first-year promotional annual card prices, credit allotments, and the first-period promo rule. Unknown: OpenArt credits per clip, so no OpenArt $/s; Higgsfield Free complimentary generations and the “selected” free models; how many official Kling app credits a clip uses; a Higgsfield plan rate for Seedance 2.5, Gemini Omni Flash, or Runway Gen-4; and a current official Google Gemini API rate for Veo 3.1, because those catalog rows are marked discontinued (discontinued on 2026-10-22).

How do we calculate this?

Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page (https://vidfare.com/about/).
